name: @guardbee/mcp-a2a-auditor
description: MCP server that scans Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol implementation code for anti-patterns found in the reference SDKs and sample agents: unauthenticated push-notification webhook fetches (SSRF), Agent Cards with no authentication requirement, and credentials embedded in publicly-served Agent Card metadata
long_description: Google's Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol is the emerging standard for agent-to-agent communication, and it has no MCP-style Security Considerations section yet. This package audits an agent's own A2A implementation against anti-patterns found by reading the reference SDKs (@a2a-js/sdk, a2a-sdk) and their official sample code directly: a push-notification webhook URL supplied by the subscribing client and fetched with no host allowlist (SSRF, present in the reference push-notification sender itself), an Agent Card with empty securitySchemes/securityRequirements or a Python AgentCard(...) missing both kwargs (no authentication requirement at all — the exact shape the SDK's own sample agent ships with), a request handler wired up with UserBuilder.noAuthentication, and a literal API key or token embedded directly in Agent Card metadata (which is served publicly at /.well-known/agent-card.json, readable by anyone). No API key required — runs entirely locally, static analysis only.
